clue.text: Harassed doctor went into digs outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the lodging word wraps round the medical letters

parts.note: to board is to lodge in digs, so having gone into lodgings is boarded
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A physician took up lodgings while being pestered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went into' looks like a container signal, but it belongs to the phrase for BOARDED; 'outside' is the real indicator. Digs are British rented lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombard someone with questions or demands is to pester them relentlessly.

clue.text: O, write a song of the great outdoors!

parts.note: to pen is to write
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A poetic apostrophe urging someone to compose a nature song.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-air takes place outside, in nature rather than indoors.

clue.text: Flatness of colour in a long beam

indicators.note: in places the colour word inside the beam word

parts.note: a boom is a long spar, as on a sail
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A description of a long beam with a dull, even colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is tedium, a flat dullness of spirit.

clue.text: Army regiment laid up-for such treatment?

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word laid is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers of a regiment are bedridden and need care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses LAID to DIAL. 'Laid up' reads as ill in bed, which suits remedial care.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial work is intended to cure or correct, describing curative care.

clue.text: Man in a mask-double one, for example

definitions.meaning: a masquerade cloak with a half-mask, and by extension its wearer
the double one is a tile in the game played with spotted tiles

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the masked carnival costume or its wearer, and a spotted gaming tile such as double one.

clue.text: They run starkers, wantonly, about the end of June

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the extra letter
wantonly suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged
the end of picks the final letter of the month

explanation.surface: Naked runners dash about in midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wantonly' rearranges STARKERS, and 'about' wraps that round E, the end of June. Starkers is British slang for naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Streakers dash naked through public places, so they are people who run.

clue.text: Muscle that moves up and down? No, about an axis

indicators.note: in a down light, reading the same up and down signals a word identical in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Asking whether a muscle works vertically, then answering that it turns round an axis.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reads the same top to bottom as bottom to top; 'No, about an axis' reminds us the muscle actually turns a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a muscle that turns a limb or body part about its axis.

clue.text: Draw at Maltese resort

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A draw played out at a holiday spot on Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a stalemate is a drawn position, and more broadly any deadlock.

clue.text: No mail going into this distant depot?

definitions.text: No mail going into this distant depot?

parts.words: No mail going into this distant depot?
parts.note: read as a post where letters only go out, never in: a remote station far from home

explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote station or settlement far from the main base.

clue.text: Request border with earth and soil

parts.note: to beg is to request
a rim is an edge or border
E is the abbreviation for earth, in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A gardener asks for an edging with earth and soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrime is to make dirty, to soil with grime.

clue.text: In which cold sheets are thrown off?

definitions.text: In which cold sheets are thrown off?

parts.words: In which cold sheets are thrown off?
parts.note: pictures frozen sheets tumbling down a glacier, not bedding thrown off on a chilly night

explanation.definitionFit: An icefall is a steep stretch of glacier where blocks of ice break and tumble.

clue.text: Ship's crew below with utter ease

parts.note: hands are crew members on a ship
down means below

explanation.surface: Sailors go below deck with no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To win hands down is to win easily, with no effort at all.

clue.text: Beat favourite dog

parts.note: to whip is to beat
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Thrashing a beloved dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The whippet is a slender racing dog breed.

clue.text: Parasite ready-made for baiting?

definitions.meaning: read as a worm already on the hook, ready for fishing

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an intestinal parasitic worm, and humorously a worm fixed on a fishing hook as bait.

clue.text: War-zone violation, opening ammunition

parts.note: a crime is a violation of the law

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A breach in a combat area: the first shots fired.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crimean War was fought there in the 1850s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimea peninsula was the scene of the Crimean War and more recent conflict.

clue.text: Where people meet after putting hammer on line

indicators.note: the hammer word is put first with the line word placed on after it
this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer

parts.note: a club is a heavy striking weapon, like a hammer
a house is a family line, a dynasty

explanation.surface: Golfers gather after holing a putt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' suggests golf, apt for a clubhouse, but here it means placing.
explanation.definitionFit: A clubhouse is the building where members of a club gather socially.

clue.text: He comport clumsily as a light, delicate sort?

indicators.note: clumsily signals the letters are put together awkwardly in a new order

explanation.surface: A slight, dainty person behaves awkwardly.
explanation.definitionFit: An ectomorph is a person of lean, slightly built body type.

clue.text: He will applaud a bell-ringer

definitions.meaning: the tongue inside a bell that strikes it

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: one who claps in approval, and the striker hanging inside a bell.

clue.text: A steward travelling to the orient

indicators.note: travelling suggests movement, so the letters shift about

explanation.surface: An airline steward flying out to Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastward means towards the east, and the orient is the east.

clue.text: Whole number, for example, in Bury

indicators.note: in places the example abbreviation inside the burial word

parts.note: to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: A whole number found in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also a town in Greater Manchester, hence the capital letter disguising a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number with no fractional part.

clue.text: Long a feature of Chesterfield-praise be-twisted!

indicators.note: a mock-archaic call for the word to be twisted, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation honouring Chesterfield's famous crooked church spire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a feature of Chesterfield' is a second cryptic hint: A SPIRE, as the town's church has a famous twisted spire.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to long for or yearn after something.

clue.text: Neat bird model

parts.note: pat means neat, glibly tidy
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A tidy bird serving as a template.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a template or model to be copied.

clue.text: Red rose embroidered for the choir-screen

indicators.note: embroidered implies the threads are worked into a new design

explanation.surface: A red rose stitched onto church hangings.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Hobo mien may produce easy good nature

indicators.note: may produce suggests the letters can be worked into something new

explanation.surface: A tramp's demeanour shows cheerful geniality.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful friendliness and geniality.

clue.text: Topics of children on Sunday?

parts.note: issue means offspring, children

explanation.surface: What children discuss on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Issues are subjects or matters under discussion.

clue.text: Wait outside coach, according to law

indicators.note: outside means the waiting word wraps round the coaching word

parts.note: to stay is to wait
a tutor is a coach

explanation.surface: Waiting outside a bus, as legally required.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutory means required or fixed by statute, the written law.

clue.text: Individual turning sour can be burdensome

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A person going sour becomes hard to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is heavy and troublesome, a burden.

clue.text: Accountant advances money on the first of every month no longer

definitions.text: the first of every month no longer

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
to lend is to advance money

explanation.surface: An accountant makes loans on the first of each month.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman calendar named the first day of each month the calends; 'no longer' marks it as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old Roman calendar the calends was the opening day of each month.

clue.text: Costly, the French article that supports 20?

parts.note: steep means expensive
le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: An expensive French item holding up another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to the answer at 20 across, the tall pointed top a church tower carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the church tower on which a spire stands.

clue.text: Shabby condition of side-sense a change?

indicators.note: a change means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a feeling at one's flank has shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Seediness is a shabby, run-down, disreputable state.
